newsitem.title: USA: Ship jam as Los Angeles harbor pilots strike.
newsitem.headline: Ship jam as Los Angeles harbor pilots strike.

text.p: A shipping logjam snarled traffic at the busiest port on the U.S. West Coast on Monday as pilots went on strike for more pay.
With 11 ships waiting to be unloaded at the Port of Los Angeles, seven more were anchored outside the harbor and three more were heading for the harbor, said Port spokeswoman Barbara Yamamoto.
The problem was exacerbated because some 3,000 dockers were refusing to cross the pilots' picket lines.

In an effort to end the impasse, the city of Los Angeles said it would ask a judge on Tuesday to order the dozen striking pilots back to work. City spokesman Keith Comrie said the legal action was in response to the pilots not negotiating in good faith.
"They're refusing to talk," said Comrie, after a meeting of the city's Executive Employee Relations Committee, which includes Mayor Richard Riordan and four city council members.
The mayor told reporters: "The bottom line is we've offered them what we've offered -- and it has been accepted by other workers in Los Angeles.
"It's highly reasonable and they should get to work."
There was no immediate comment from the pilots' union, the International Longshore and Warehouse Union.
The pilots were seeking a 72 percent pay raise from $113,712 to $195,000 over two years to bring them in line, they say, with pilots in other U.S. ports.
The city has offered a four-year package amounting to a 17 percent raise to $133,000 in salary plus overtime and other benefits, including a retirement plan.
